orderBook.title: Order book and new bookings
orderBook.content:
The order book is the US-dollar value of signed, uncancelled newbuild contracts not yet delivered -- the shipyard's revenue backlog. New bookings is the value of contracts signed in the period, which refills (or shrinks) that backlog.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the order book stood at US$22.4bn (245 vessels) at FY2025 year-end, extending revenue visibility to 2030 with shipyard capacity largely committed through H2 2029. The green/dual-fuel share of order book value rose from 58% (FY2023) to 71% (FY2025) as the global fleet shifts to meet IMO emissions rules -- a mix shift that supports pricing even if gross tonnage growth slows.

What to watch:

  • Bookings falling below deliveries (the order book shrinking) -- new order intake fell sharply in FY2025 off a record FY2024
  • Order book coverage (years of forward revenue) narrowing as yard capacity gets worked through to 2029-2030
  • Pricing per vessel/CGT holding up versus a cyclical newbuild-price peak

deliveries.title: Vessels delivered
deliveries.content:
New units delivered is the count of vessels handed over to customers in the year -- each delivery converts order-book backlog into recognised revenue and milestone cash.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: deliveries were 57 vessels in FY2023 and 56 in FY2025, roughly steady even as the order book nearly tripled by value -- consistent with rising average contract price and vessel complexity (LNG/LPG carriers, larger containerships) rather than higher throughput.

What to watch:

  • Delivery count against order-book depletion -- flat deliveries with a growing backlog implies a lengthening queue, not necessarily more capacity
  • Yard utilisation and any slippage/delay disclosures around delivery dates

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings) Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: The automated sanity_check.py script flagged this DCF passed: false, but that is a known, documented, out-of-scope-to-fix bug in the checker itself, not a problem with the valuation. The checker mixes the SGD share quote with RMB financials without correctly bridging the fx_rate (0.1911 RMB→SGD), which corrupts its printed implied/historical P/E, P/B and EV/EBITDA multiples into nonsense. The dcf-analyst hand-bridged the real numbers (RMB-per-share × 0.1911 = SGD-per-share) across FY2016-FY2025: at the current price (SGD 4.88), P/E is 11.65x and P/B is 3.13x — both above the real 10-year historical maximum (P/E 9.51x, P/B 2.40x). At the base-case intrinsic value (SGD 3.13), P/E is 7.47x and P/B is 2.01x — comfortably inside the historical range. This is consistent with, not contradicted by, the DCF's own base case: shipbuilding margins and the order book are near a cyclical peak, which is exactly why the base case calls for -35% downside to intrinsic value. No drivers were changed to work around the checker.
